q1.label: Are the image quality and view adequate to judge the answer?
q1.help:
Judge only image quality and view.
Yes: good enough to judge the whole answer.
Partly: good enough for only part of the answer (for example, part of the structure is out of view). Judge only that part.
No: the image quality or view is too poor to judge any part of the answer. This ends the record.

q2.label: Is the question–answer pair itself valid? Tick all that apply.
q2.help: Recorded separately from Q1; continue to Q3–Q4 even if not valid.

options.unanswerable: Question cannot be answered from the image and the information in the question
options.off_topic: Answer does not address the question

q3.label: Is the answer accurate? Tick all that apply.
q3.help:
Accurate: nothing is wrong, over-stated or missing. It cannot be combined with the other options.
Wrong: something stated is incorrect: a finding that is not in the image, the location or side, the description or diagnosis, or a measurement or count.
Over-stated: the answer goes beyond the evidence (neither the image nor the question supports it), or is more certain than the evidence allows; for example "biopsy-proven" when the question gives no pathology, or "malignant" where only suspicious features are seen. Citing history or pathology that the question itself provides is not over-stated.
Under-stated: an important finding within the question's scope is missing (tricky case 1).
Q3 is about the words only; a mask on the wrong structure is recorded in Q4. Use the standard lexicon (BI-RADS, TI-RADS) where one exists.

q4.label: Records with a mask only: do the question, the answer text and the mask point to the same target?
q4.help: Check only that they refer to the same target; no pixel-level check of the outline is needed. A mask on the wrong structure is recorded here only (Q4 = "No"), not in Q3.

optional.intro: These help us describe the errors but do not change the three outcome classes. Leave them blank if you are short of time.

error_types.label: Error type (E1–E7)
error_types.help: When Q3 is Wrong, Over-stated or Under-stated, you can add the error types (see Error types): Wrong = E1, E3, E4, E6; Over-stated = E5, E7; Under-stated = E2.

significance.label: Clinical significance
significance.help: Likely significant = likely to change interpretation, management or triage (tricky case 3). Use "Not applicable (phantom)" only for phantom images; phantom images are still judged for accuracy in Q3 as usual (tricky case 9).

quote.label: Quoted words
quote.help: When you tick Over-stated, quoting the words is recommended but not required.

note.label: Case note
note.help: Use it for any problem that the questions above do not cover. For records outside your experience, write "needs specialist review" in the note.
